App::PropertyBoolList.setter: bool | int | Iterable[bool | int] | dict[int, bool | int] | str
App::PropertyBoolList.note: Getter builds a tuple. Setter accepts binary-digit strings via dynamic_bitset; other inputs follow PropertyListsT conversion. A single bool/int replaces with one item, iterables replace contents, and integer-key dictionaries update/append indexed items. Index -1 or current length appends.

App::PropertyColorList.note: Getter builds RGBA tuples. Each setter item is converted by PropertyColor::setPyObject; inherited PropertyListsT also accepts a single color, iterables, and indexed dictionaries. _ColorInput is defined in conversion-aliases.md.

App::PropertyMaterial.note: Getter creates a material copy. Setter accepts legacy App MaterialPy or MaterialPy::toColor inputs: packed integer or homogeneous integer/float RGB/RGBA tuple. FreeCAD.Material is distinct from the modern Materials.Material API.

App::PropertyMaterialList.note: Getter builds a tuple of material copies. Inherited PropertyListsT handles scalar, iterable, and indexed updates; getPyValue accepts only MaterialPy, unlike PropertyMaterial's color shortcut. The native class maintains a minimum list size of one.

App::PropertyRotation.note: Getter constructs a copy; Matrix assignment extracts rotation and Rotation assignment copies its value.

App::PropertyMatrix.note: Getter copies the matrix. Tuple setter requires exactly 16 numbers and fills cMatrix[x][y] from tuple[x + y*4]; do not assume row-major ordering or accept lists.

App::PropertyIntegerSet.note: Getter returns a set; setter accepts a scalar integer or PySequence_Check sequence of integers. A Python set is not accepted merely because it is the getter result; assign list(result) when round-tripping.

App::PropertyPythonObject.note: Getter returns a new reference to the stored arbitrary Python object, not a copy. Setter stores that object with native change notification. This conversion does not establish that every object is persistable.

App::PropertyPath.note: Filesystem path conversion uses a UTF-8 Python string. This is distinct from CAM's Path::PropertyPath toolpath.

App::PropertyXLinkSubList.setter: PropertyLinkSub input or list/tuple of PropertyLinkSub inputs
App::PropertyXLinkSubList.note: Getter skips absent/detached linked objects. Setter first tries PropertyLinkSub syntax with external links allowed, then a tuple/list of such inputs; it groups subnames by object. PropertyLinkSub input includes an object, None, or object/subname pair. Cross-document and runtime attachment state remain relevant.

Inspection::PropertyDistanceList.note: This setter checks PyList/PyFloat explicitly; integer entries and general iterable/tuple inputs are not accepted by this implementation.

Part::PropertyFilletEdges.note: Canonical setter form is a sequence of edge-id, first-radius, second-radius tuples. C++ PyCXX conversion reads tuple items 0..2; this describes the supported form without promising exact rejection/coercion behavior for every malformed input.

Part::PropertyShapeHistory.note: Getter always returns None and setter is empty. Python assignment does not alter the native history; this property is not an exposed shape-history editing API.

Mesh::PropertyCurvatureList.getter: list[tuple[float, float, tuple[float, float, float], tuple[float, float, float]]]
Mesh::PropertyCurvatureList.note: Each entry is maximum curvature, minimum curvature, maximum direction xyz, minimum direction xyz. Setter unconditionally raises a read-only AttributeError.

Points::PropertyPointKernel.note: Getter wraps the stored point kernel and calls setConst; setter copies an accepted PointsPy kernel. Reassign a separately constructed Points.Points value for edits.

Path::PropertyPath.note: Getter copies the toolpath into PathPy; setter accepts PathPy and copies its Toolpath. Module initialization exports the wrapper as Path.Path.

Robot::PropertyTrajectory.note: Getter copies the trajectory into TrajectoryPy; setter accepts that wrapper and copies the value. Module initialization exports Robot.Trajectory.

Fem::PropertyFemMesh.note: Getter wraps the stored mesh and calls setConst. A mesh setter copies the mesh; a Placement setter transforms existing mesh geometry, rather than storing placement as the property value.

Fem::PropertyPostDataObject.getter: VTK Python data-object wrapper when FC_USE_VTK_PYTHON is enabled
Fem::PropertyPostDataObject.setter: VTK Python object convertible to vtkDataObject when FC_USE_VTK_PYTHON is enabled
Fem::PropertyPostDataObject.note: Getter wraps a deep-copied dataset; setter checks vtkDataObject and deep-copies it. Without FC_USE_VTK_PYTHON, both directions signal NotImplementedError. Actual VTK Python class and supported concrete dataset subtype depend on the build/value; they are intentionally not flattened into one unconditional Python signature.

SketcherGui::PropertyVisualLayerList.setter: nonempty values raise NotImplementedError; no supported Python counterpart
SketcherGui::PropertyVisualLayerList.note: getPyObject and per-item getPyValue explicitly throw because there is no Python counterpart. Inherited empty-list operations may avoid per-item conversion, but are not a supported visual-layer editing contract. Use the documented Sketcher/view-provider methods instead of inventing a Python VisualLayer value.

App::DocumentObject.note: This implementation creates DocumentObjectPy. Its binding is FreeCAD.DocumentObject; descendant overrides must be checked before claiming the same returned Python type.

App::GeoFeature.note: This implementation creates GeoFeaturePy. The binding is FreeCAD.GeoFeature; native descendants may override getPyObject.

Part::Feature.note: This implementation creates PartFeaturePy, exposed as Part.Feature. Descendant overrides, including Primitive and FeaturePython, are separate implementations.

Part::Primitive.note: Handwritten PrimitivePy derives from PartFeaturePy. No independent public Part.Primitive import is established by this review.

Part::Box.note: Box declares no getPyObject override; its native chain reaches Primitive::getPyObject and PrimitivePy. This source-backed inherited wrapper evidence does not establish a public Part.Box class.

App::FeaturePython.note: Explicit specialization constructs FeaturePythonPyT<DocumentObjectPy>. A proxy object is distinct from this returned native wrapper; no standalone FreeCAD.FeaturePython import is promised.

Part::FeaturePython.note: Explicit specialization constructs FeaturePythonPyT<Part::PartFeaturePy>. This is a native feature wrapper with a Python Proxy, not the proxy's Python class.

Gui::ViewProvider.note: This implementation creates ViewProviderPy; the public binding is FreeCADGui.ViewProvider. GUI-only and descendant overrides still apply.

Gui::ViewProviderDocumentObject.note: This implementation requires the main thread and creates ViewProviderDocumentObjectPy; the binding is FreeCADGui.ViewProviderDocumentObject. It does not prove that every derived view provider returns this exact wrapper.
